correctness.rationale: For each row, the normal equation gives e_i=(h^T g_i)/||g_i||^2. Gaussian orthogonality makes h independent of the correlated g_i. Its one-row squared error is F_{1,q}/q. In the distinct-line case the 2q-dimensional Gaussian joint density at zero, after scaling g_i by sqrt(t), yields t^{-q} times an explicit two-ball integral. Cauchy--Schwarz bounds each scaled sketch vector by ||h||, so dominated convergence follows from the finite 2q-th Gaussian moment. The polar integral J_q(h) and radial chi moment produce K_q, with all constants checked independently. At exact alignment g_2=+/-g_1 and Y_2=Y_1, giving exponent q/2. Individual error means are finite for q>=3. The finite numerical suite (2,759 assertions) checks the algebra and constants but is not the proof.

originality.rationale: The 2026 Algorithm 1 establishes expected Frobenius error and Markov bounds, and the 2024 fixed-sparsity precursor similarly addresses expectation/probability bounds. Prior Gaussian sketch inference already covers the one-row Student distribution, which is explicitly excluded from novelty. The candidate instead asserts an exact simultaneous two-row catastrophic-tail coefficient for heterogeneous row spaces and a discontinuous exponent at alignment. Searches of mathematical literature and published mathematical records for joint ratios, Gaussian sketches and angle-dependent extreme probabilities found related but non-equivalent results. Novelty is a best-knowledge self-review rather than an independence or exhaustive-priority guarantee.
residual_risks: Older specialized joint-tail theorems for correlated Gaussian self-normalized ratios may contain equivalent or stronger asymptotics not located by the bounded search.
The asymptotic is for fixed nonaligned rho; a near-alignment crossover at a rho that depends on threshold is not established.
Proof is self-reviewed; no independent scientific audit or external priority certification.

value.rationale: A shared nonadaptive query matrix is reused across differently oriented row subspaces in the motivating numerical algorithm. Individual row risks are identical at every angle, so marginal Student guarantees and expected Frobenius error are insensitive to a structural risk variable. The theorem gives the sharp simultaneous catastrophic-failure rate, its explicit angle coefficient and singular aligned exponent, showing that even orthogonal row-space templates retain correlated rare-event risk. This is a motivated complete fixed-angle classification for two-row shared-residual configurations and a meaningful reliability boundary, not an arbitrary parameter-table exercise. It does not claim a full multirank operator guarantee.
